hypothesis: KDA stage 2 reaches every logical chunk through a runtime start offset: it pads the packed time axis, materializes each BT tile with a vmapped dynamic_slice, and scatter-adds the kernel outputs back through an [NC, BT] int32 position vector. chunk_kda_fwd always hands that stage a varlen-aligned layout in which chunk c is exactly rows [c*BT, (c+1)*BT), so a contiguous chunk-block schedule can re-block it by reshape: no tile copy, no int32 position vector, no T+BT scatter buffer. That removes the DMA-bound index/copy segments the campaign attributes to kda-long while returning bit-identical tensors.

estimate.reasoning: The aggregate objective is 3.349ms (tiny-linear-serving is the only model with a plan; the dense/MoE callsites are deferred). The action's two affected callsites are 50.5% of it: kda-long 1.133ms = 33.8% and kda-short 0.560ms = 16.7%. UPPER BOUND from the campaign L1 panel: 35% of kda-long sits in two int32 index segments (#47 22% + #42 13%, cmp=0%/bw=100%) and 11% more in a float32 rank-3 segment -- exactly the pos/flat_pos position vectors and the per-chunk gather/scatter tile copies. Stage 2 owns roughly half that machinery (stage 2 issues 5 gathers + 4 live scatter-adds, stage 4 issues 4 gathers + 1), i.e. ~23% of kda-long, giving 0.338*23 + 0.167*12 = 9.8%. LOWER BOUND from a full 420-configuration timing sweep of both KDA cases on this round's GPU-interpret proxy: the best deployable config improves from 0.9998ms to 0.9556ms (4.42%) on kda-long and from 0.4110ms to 0.4054ms (1.36%) on kda-short -- both at the unchanged incumbent knob settings -- i.e. 0.338*4.42 + 0.167*1.36 = 1.7%. That denominator is inflated because every Pallas stage runs interpreted here, while the deleted work (about 18MB of HBM traffic per kda-long call -- the T+BT pads, the per-chunk gather copies and the zero-initialized scatter buffers -- plus 9 dynamic-index operations) is unchanged by interpretation. The estimate takes a conservative 8% local relief on kda-long and 4% on kda-short, inside those bounds: 0.338*8 + 0.167*4 = 2.7 + 0.7 = 3.4%.

hypothesis: The GLA recurrent-state stage launches its Pallas grid as (H, K/BK, V/BV, NT) and only the chunk axis is sequential -- the head axis is pure parallelism that carries no data between programs. Every head therefore pays a full program prologue, grid bookkeeping, boundary-scalar read (chunk_to_seq, bos, eos, seq_real_lens) and its own narrow k/v tile transfer to run one [BK,BT]x[BT,BV] state update. A head-grouped schedule gives one program HEAD_GROUP adjacent heads, each keeping its own recurrent scratch plane and its own unchanged arithmetic, so the boundary scalars are read once per group and the k/v tiles arrive as one wider transfer instead of HEAD_GROUP separate ones. Head arithmetic is never mixed, so the emitted per-head states and final states are the incumbent's.

estimate.reasoning: The paired incumbent aggregate is 3.358ms and tiny-linear-serving is the only model with a plan. The action's two affected callsites are 53.2% of it: gla-long 1.097ms = 32.7% and gla-short 0.689ms = 20.5%. LOCALIZATION: a stage decomposition of the incumbent-selected plans on this round's GPU-interpret proxy puts chunk_fwd_h_kernel_varlen at 0.537ms of gla-long's 1.082ms (49.7%) and 0.514ms of gla-short's 0.693ms (74.2%) -- the single largest stage at both callsites, and the stage this action schedules. A grid-program scaling sweep isolates the cause: state-stage latency is 58-89us per grid program and is flat in tile size (H=8,T=2048,cs=2048 -> 8 programs -> 0.555ms; H=8,T=512,cs=512 -> 8 programs -> 0.501ms; H=1 -> 1 program -> 0.089ms at both shapes), i.e. the stage is per-program overhead bound, not work bound. Grouping G heads per program divides the program count by G, so the relief is a schedule property rather than an arithmetic saving. MEASURED UPPER REFERENCE: a full 2x112-configuration deployable sweep of both GLA cases on the proxy takes the best deployable config from 1.0091ms to 0.8151ms on gla-long (19.22%, both at chunk_size=2048/compact_alignment=True/output_value_tiles=4) and from 0.6279ms to 0.5008ms on gla-short (20.25%, chunk_size=512/compact_alignment=True/output_value_tiles=8), i.e. 0.327*19.22 + 0.205*20.25 = 6.3 + 4.2 = 10.4% aggregate; all 224 configurations stayed correct. That denominator is inflated for the target: the interpret proxy pays a Python-level grid loop per program, so it exaggerates the fixed per-program cost that Mosaic amortizes in hardware. The estimate discounts the measured local relief by roughly 40% to 11% on gla-long and 12% on gla-short, which are still above the residual grid/prologue cost a real Pallas launch pays per program: 0.327*11 + 0.205*12 = 3.6 + 2.5 = 6.0%.
